title: Microchip MTCH3380P and MTCH3240P capacitive touch controllers support up to 64 buttons with parallel sensing
summary: Microchip Technology has introduced the MTCH3380P and MTCH3240P, two new capacitive touch controllers that handle touch detection internally, making it easier to build display-free HMI devices with touch-sensitive buttons, sliders, and wheels. The main difference between the two controllers is the number of supported touch sensors. The MTCH3380P supports up to 38 self-capacitance or 64 mutual-capacitance keys, while the smaller MTCH3240P supports up to 24 self-capacitance or 32 mutual-capacitance keys. Both controllers use parallel sensing with 12 on-chip ADCs to improve touch response times and noise immunity. They also support touch detection through thick cover materials and when users are wearing gloves, making them suitable for home appliances, industrial control panels, EV chargers, and outdoor kiosks. Both also support IEC/UL 60730 Class B functional safety requirements. Microchip MTCH3380P and MTCH3240P specifications: Controller engine Microchip patented charge-transfer acquisition engine with pipelined analog sensing and digital processing. The new Fixed Wireless Access (FWA) solution features a Qualcomm X105 Modem-RF with 5G NR over satellite support, quad-frequency GNSS (L1, L2, L5, and L6), Qualcomm Turbo DSDA for 60% higher throughput compared to Gen 5, a quad-core CPU, an integrated 10 TOPS NPU, LPDDR4x and LPDDR5/5x, and quantum security (CNSA 2.0 compliant). It offers 500 MHz of aggregated bandwidth, 6- and 8-layer MIMO, peak download and upload speeds of 14.8 Gbps and 4.2 Gbps, respectively.
